primers.title: The resilience_level dial: what 0, 1 and 2 buy
primers.body_md:
`resilience_level` is one coarse dial that abstracts away the choice of method, leaving a cost/accuracy trade. The validator accepts only 0, 1 and 2; a string `"2"` or `2.0` is silently coerced.

| Level | What it applies | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | no mitigation at all | none |
| 1 (the default) | readout mitigation via Twirled Readout Error eXtinction (TREX): measurement twirling plus an inversion of the diagonalized readout-error transfer matrix | minimal |
| 2 | everything level 1 does, PLUS zero-noise extrapolation and gate twirling | medium; typically reduces bias, but "not guaranteed to be zero-bias" |

There is no level 3, and no level turns on PEC — only `resilience.pec_mitigation` does. A higher level post-processes a larger ensemble of related circuits: more accurate, less biased expectation values for longer processing time and more QPU usage. It never makes a job cheaper, faster or shallower, nor changes which physical qubits you land on.

Options you set are applied IN ADDITION to the level's base set: level 0 turns `zne_mitigation` off, yet an explicit `resilience.zne_mitigation = True` re-enables ZNE.

Suppression versus mitigation:

| Family | When it acts | Examples | How you switch it on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| error suppression | before or during execution, to stop errors happening | dynamical decoupling pulses idling qubits so their idle-time errors approximately cancel | `options.dynamical_decoupling.enable` |
| error mitigation | after execution, post-processing an ensemble of circuits to remove bias from expectation values | TREX, ZNE, PEA, PEC | `resilience_level` or `resilience.*_mitigation` |
| neither | — | a higher transpiler optimization level; more shots, which shrink the STATISTICAL error, not the systematic bias | — |

primers.title: The EstimatorOptions tree and its defaults
primers.body_md:
`EstimatorOptions` is a nested dataclass; most option questions test nesting DEPTH.

| Level | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| top | `max_execution_time`, `environment`, `simulator`, `default_precision`, `default_shots`, `resilience_level`, `seed_estimator`, `dynamical_decoupling`, `resilience`, `execution`, `twirling`, `experimental` |
| `resilience` | `measure_mitigation`, `measure_noise_learning`, `zne_mitigation`, `zne`, `pec_mitigation`, `pec`, `layer_noise_learning`, `layer_noise_model` |
| `resilience.zne` | `amplifier`, `noise_factors`, `extrapolator`, `extrapolated_noise_factors` |

Three mistakes: the WRONG NAME (`zne.factors`, the Mitiq-flavoured `zne.scale_factors`), the right name at the WRONG LEVEL, and CONFIGURING WITHOUT ENABLING. Setting `resilience.zne.noise_factors` is accepted but leaves `zne_mitigation` at `Unset`, so the job runs without ZNE; `resilience.zne_mitigation.enable = True` raises nothing — `Unset` is a plain singleton, so the write lands harmlessly on it.

| Technique | Turned on only by |
| --- | --- |
| ZNE | `resilience.zne_mitigation = True` (or `resilience_level = 2`) |
| TREX | `resilience.measure_mitigation = True` |
| PEC | `resilience.pec_mitigation = True` |

Documented defaults ("what if I touch nothing"):

| Option | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `resilience_level` | 1 |
| `resilience.measure_mitigation` | True |
| `resilience.zne_mitigation`, `resilience.pec_mitigation` | False |
| `resilience.zne.noise_factors` | (1, 3, 5) |
| `resilience.zne.amplifier` | `gate_folding` |
| `resilience.zne.extrapolator` | (exponential, linear) |
| `dynamical_decoupling.enable`, `sequence_type` | False, `XX` |
| `twirling.enable_gates`, `twirling.enable_measure` | False, True |
| `default_precision` | 0.015625 — exactly 1/sqrt(4096) |
| `max_execution_time` | 10800 seconds |

An untouched option sits at `Unset`: the server default applies. Set values with an `EstimatorOptions` instance or nested dict at construction, attribute-path assignment, or a bulk `options.update(...)`.

primers.title: The Estimator PUB: four positional slots
primers.body_md:
An Estimator PUB is a tuple of AT MOST FOUR values in positional slots, never matched by content.

| Slot | Contents | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | one `QuantumCircuit` | may contain `Parameter` objects |
| 2 | an array of one or more observables | anything `ObservablesArrayLike`: `Pauli`, `SparsePauliOp`, `PauliList` or a bare string |
| 3 | parameter values to bind | its LAST index runs over the circuit's parameters; omit it or pass `None` when the circuit has none |
| 4 | a target precision (optional) | a float dropped into slot 3 gives `ValueError: Length of () inconsistent with last dimension of [0.01]` |

```python
result = est.run([(isa, isa_obs, params, 0.01)])   # not est.run((isa, isa_obs))
```

NumPy broadcasting of the observables array against the parameter-value array decides the output: one expectation value per element of the broadcast shape.

| Observables | Parameter values | `evs.shape` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| one observable | none | `()` |
| flat list `[o1, o2, o3]` | none | `(3,)` |
| column `[[o1], [o2], [o3]]` | none | `(3, 1)` |
| row `[[o1, o2, o3]]` | none | `(1, 3)` |
| one observable | `(4, 1)` | `(4,)` |
| a `(4, 1)` column | `(1, 6)` | `(4, 6)` |

A `SparsePauliOp` is a SINGLE element however many terms it holds: one number, the coefficient-weighted sum. Commuting observables share a measurement only within the SAME PUB; two PUBs mean two measurement bases.

The `PrimitiveResult` holds one `PubResult` per PUB. `result[0].data` is a `DataBin` with exactly `evs` and `stds`, both real `float64`; `metadata` holds only `target_precision` and `circuit_metadata`.

primers.title: Observables, layout alignment, and precision
primers.body_md:
An n-qubit observable is a weighted sum of Pauli tensor products, which `SparsePauliOp` stores. Only I and Z are diagonal in the measurement basis; the Estimator automatically changes basis for X (H) and Y (S-dagger then H).

| Constructor | Takes | Watch for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SparsePauliOp(['ZZ', 'XX'], coeffs=[1.0, 0.5])` | labels plus `coeffs`, width inferred from the labels | there is no `num_qubits=` keyword here |
| `SparsePauliOp.from_list([('ZZ', 1.0), ('XX', 0.5)])` | (label, coefficient) pairs on FULL-WIDTH labels | mixing widths raises `ValueError: The Nth Pauli is defined over k qubits` |
| `SparsePauliOp.from_sparse_list([('Z', [0], 1.0)], num_qubits=3)` | (label, qubit_indices, coefficient) triples plus `num_qubits` | `num_qubits` is REQUIRED here, and the result is padded with identities to `'IIZ'` |

Transpiling pads the circuit to full backend width and may permute qubits; the observable does not follow, so align it: `isa_observable = observable.apply_layout(isa_circuit.layout)`. `measure_all()`, a string observable or `initial_layout=[0, 1]` do not help — the circuit stays at full backend width.

`precision` is a target STANDARD ERROR, not a shot count, hence a float. Statistical error falls as 1/sqrt(N), so shot cost goes as 1/precision^2.

| Rank | Where the precision comes from |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | a precision inside the PUB |
| 2 | `run(precision=...)` |
| 3 | twirling being on by default, `num_randomizations` × `shots_per_randomization` |
| 4 | `default_shots` |
| 5 | `default_precision`, documented as 0.015625 = 1/sqrt(4096) |

The requested precision is not GUARANTEED, and lower precision costs more QPU time.

facts.fact_md: ZNE runs the circuit at amplified noise rates (digital gate folding) and extrapolates to the zero-noise limit; it "is not guaranteed to produce an unbiased result".

PEC writes the ideal circuit as a quasi-probability combination of noisy ones: unbiased, but its sampling overhead scales quadratically in gamma = sum of |quasi-probabilities|, which grows exponentially with depth.
PEC is incompatible with gate-folding ZNE, PEA and fractional gates; enabling `pec_mitigation` with `zne_mitigation` raises a validation error.

`default_precision` sets error-bar length: 0.1 gives `stds` around 0.04–0.10 on a fake backend, 0.01 around 0.002–0.009. `options.execution.shots` is no route — `execution` holds only `init_qubits` and `rep_delay`.
`resilience_level` values `3`, `4`, `5`, `-1` and `1.5` all raise a pydantic `ValidationError` about the 0..2 range.
ZNE scale factors live at `options.resilience.zne.noise_factors`; `zne.factors` (wrong name) and `resilience.noise_factors` (wrong level) are `no_such_attribute` errors.
`default_precision` must be strictly positive: `0` raises `ValidationError` whether assigned or passed as `EstimatorOptions(default_precision=0)`.
`EstimatorV2.run()` takes only `precision=`; `shots=`, `default_precision=` and `resilience_level=` raise `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument`, and `options.precision` a `ValidationError`.

A 2-qubit observable against a 5-qubit ISA circuit raises `ValueError: The number of qubits of the circuit (5) does not match the number of qubits of the ()-th observable (2)`; only `obs.apply_layout(isa.layout)` fixes it.
`SparsePauliOp('ZZ').apply_layout([2, 0], num_qubits=4)` returns `'IZIZ'`: label characters pair with the index list left-to-right, while the printed label stays little-endian.
A multi-term `SparsePauliOp` is ONE observable: `from_list([('X', 3.0)])` on |+⟩ returns a 0-d `float64` array holding 3.0 — not a length-1 array, not one value per term.
Halving the target precision quadruples the shots: measured standard error falls from 0.0195 at 2500 shots to 0.0104 at 4x the shots; 2x only reaches 0.0137.
`result[0].data.evs` holds the estimates, `result[0].data.stds` their standard errors; `data.expectation_values` is an `AttributeError`, `metadata['evs']` a `KeyError`.

Even a single PUB must be wrapped in a list: `est.run([(isa, iobs)])`. A bare circuit raises `ValueError: An invalid Estimator pub-like was given`; the V1 `run(circuits=..., observables=...)` raises `TypeError`.
The reference `StatevectorEstimator` reports `stds` of exactly `0.0` — exact calculation, no sampling uncertainty — even when `run()` asks for a tighter precision.
Sweeping `ry(theta)` over 0 to 2π against `SparsePauliOp('Z')` traces ONE full cosine period; cos(theta/2) gives half a period, cos(2*theta) two.
A dict observable becomes ONE weighted observable: `[{'ZI': 2.0, 'IX': 1.0}, 'XZ']` gives `evs` of shape `(2,)`, the first entry 2⟨ZI⟩ + ⟨IX⟩ — never one value per dict key.

On a shot-based Estimator, precision p buys ceil(1/p²) shots (`precision=0.05` reports `metadata['shots'] == 400`), and a term's std scales as sqrt(1 − ⟨P⟩²)/sqrt(shots), so on an eigenstate of the observable `stds` is exactly 0.0.

checklist: Recite the levels: 0 no mitigation, 1 (default) TREX, 2 adds ZNE and gate twirling.
Expect a higher resilience level to cost more processing time and QPU usage, never less.
Remember options you set apply in addition to the level's base set.
Put each option at its depth — `resilience.zne.noise_factors` configures ZNE, `resilience.zne_mitigation = True` enables it.
Order an Estimator PUB: circuit, observables, parameter values, precision — wrapped in a list.
Predict `evs.shape` by broadcasting observables against parameter values; a `SparsePauliOp` is one element.
Map every observable through `obs.apply_layout(isa.layout)` before running on a transpiled circuit.
Treat `precision` as a target standard error: halving it quadruples the shots.
